answer: Consider a bond schedule keyed to payout. To claim even one unit of nectar from the reward pool, an agent must lock a bond larger than the maximum it can extract before the next checkpoint. A Sybil operator who spawns an ocean of fresh keys cannot spread that cost across cheap identities: each key carries the same locked bond, and any cluster caught voting together is slashed in full at once. The gale of one slashing event wipes the capital behind every clone. Cost scales linearly with identity count, while honest agents recover their bond, so forgery loses money.
